estimation_procedure.description: For each forecast-origin year 1969–2012 and horizon τ=1–5, estimate an annual cross-sectional regression using all available data in the previous ten years, with the horizon-specific lag alignment described by the paper. Apply the pooled coefficients to year-t firm inputs to produce forecasts for years t+1 through t+5.

estimation_procedure.description: For each forecast-origin year 1969–2012 and horizon τ=1–5, estimate an annual cross-sectional regression using all available data in the previous ten years, with the horizon-specific lag alignment described by the paper. Fit each year as of June 30; for year t, only financial statements with fiscal year ends from April of t−1 through March of t are used. Apply the pooled coefficients to year-t firm inputs to produce forecasts for years t+1 through t+5.

review_notes: Scope: as a paper developing and comparing cross-sectional earnings-forecast methods, the actual fitted HVZ, EP, and RI forecast-generating regressions are primary. Table 1 reports averaged coefficients for horizons t+1 through t+3; the text says the t+4 and t+5 fits were also estimated but are not tabulated. The parameter-free random-walk benchmark is not a fitted regression. Forecast-error, ERC, ICC-return, and ICC-risk regressions are downstream evaluations of forecast outputs and are not primary model fits.

Per-fit N is not reported for the rolling annual cross-sectional regressions. The linked sample record’s 119,653 observations describe the later common forecast-evaluation sample, not a rolling regression fit; no aggregate or evaluation N is assigned to these regressions.
descriptive_reason: The reviewed source does not report data-value descriptives for the retained forecast outcomes or predictors. Table 1 reports averages of estimated regression coefficients, not descriptive statistics of the underlying data. Other tables report forecast-error/performance measures, which are downstream quantities outside the retained baseline-variable descriptive scope.
results_review_notes: Table 1 reports only t+1, t+2, and t+3 results in the paper; the prose notes t+4 and t+5 estimates are available upon request, and they remain outside the frozen selected horizon set.

The frozen inventory encodes the selected t+1/t+2/t+3 horizons as columns, but the viewed original Table 1 presents them as outcome rows. The enrichment records the selected horizons and flags this layout discrepancy.
